sections.title: quick_answer

sections.body_md:
### The code and the additional suffix

ESFJ abbreviates Extraversion, Sensing, Feeling and Judging: attention toward external engagement, concrete information, values and human circumstances in decisions, and an inclination to arrange external life. Preferences do not score sociability, memory, empathy or organizing skill. The [base ESFJ profile](/en/personality/esfj) explains the four pairs in detail.

In the [16Personalities NERIS framework](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory), Assertive/Turbulent belongs to Identity. The Assertive account emphasizes self-assurance. [Official MBTI uses four preference pairs](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts) without this fifth label. FermatMind uses related suffix language for reflection; that does not establish equivalent instruments, classifications or validity.

The Assertive account concerns self-evaluation and responses to success or criticism, not guaranteed composure in every situation, a set recovery time or demonstrated boundary-setting skill. Confidence in a familiar task can coexist with uncertainty in an important relationship. One first response to criticism cannot classify a suffix. A framework's description or a respondent's confidence about performance is different from evidence of actual performance.

### Keep the suffix separate from function theory

Fe–Si–Ne–Ti is a common theoretical interpretation of four-letter ESFJ. Fe addresses outward interpersonal and shared values; Si reference to experience. Neither establishes accurate mind-reading, kindness or memory. Official type dynamics leaves tertiary Intuition open to Ne or Ni: one view reverses the auxiliary attitude, another reverses the dominant attitude for the other processes. The [base profile explains that disagreement](/en/personality/esfj#meaning).

A does not add a function, measure Fe development or upgrade the theory into an established mechanism. NERIS does not use Jungian function stacks. The tables and scenarios here are original educational illustrations, not findings about ESFJ-A performance or the effects of a subtype-specific intervention.
sections.title: What the letters mean

sections.body_md:
### Offer a starting point with room for a real answer

You may recognize an Assertive account when you can propose a concrete arrangement without first obtaining everyone's approval of you. A clear starting point can give others something useful to evaluate. State its purpose, known conditions, unconfirmed parts and what can be changed; feeling ready cannot establish that the recipient has everything needed.

A choice must include a workable refusal. If declining help means being treated as ungrateful or uncooperative, the offer is less open than it appears. Ask what the person wants to handle themselves, whether help is wanted and whether another time or contact is possible. They need not disclose private circumstances to earn that choice. Accepting help once is not permanent permission; no answer is not consent.

### Separate self-trust from the state of the task

| Observed event | What it does not establish | A relevant check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I think the group message is clear | The recipient saw it and can act | Current access, shift, receipt and understandable steps |
| A relative declines public birthday attention | They are ungrateful or the relationship is failing | What is welcome now and whether naming them is permitted |
| A colleague objects to my timing | My whole ability is being rejected | The specific barrier, changeable scope and decision authority |
| I feel settled again | All effects are repaired or everyone else feels settled | Agreed repairs, open commitments and any remaining concrete concern |

These are questions, not a diagnostic table. Explaining a plan can be useful, but explaining first does not replace understanding an obstacle. A preference for another format can be discussed; missing necessary access needs a relevant remedy rather than another assurance that your plan was considerate. Both can happen without turning one response into a fixed A/T identity.

### Let experience remain useful without making it unquestionable

An established reminder may work under familiar conditions. New participants, shifts, permissions or purposes can change those conditions. Hear the specific difference before choosing to retain, amend, investigate or stop the arrangement. Someone should not need repeated complaints to make a real barrier count. Revising in light of a material fact does not invalidate your entire judgment.

Uncertainty in unfamiliar work, wanting appreciation, solitary interests or declining an invitation can coexist with parts of this account. Do not force every exception into a hidden opposite type. Culture, experience, responsibility and authority also influence conduct. You need neither permanent certainty nor repeated unnecessary changes to demonstrate openness.
sections.title: Patterns, strengths and counterexamples

sections.body_md:
### Original shift example: a sent reminder still leaves access and accepted work to check

You trust a familiar group reminder, but a new worker misses an assignment. Check five separate states:

- **Access:** could the worker view the group?
- **Shift:** were they working at that time?
- **Timing:** was the current reporting time clear?
- **Steps:** were the assignment and its changes understandable?
- **Responsibility:** had the worker actually accepted the work?

 Sending the message, being able to view it, receiving it and carrying out a task are separate facts. Previous workers knowing the routine cannot settle this handoff.

Confirm a usable channel and backup contact with whoever has authority. Explain the current time, critical steps and open issues. Invite the recipient to recount their understanding to reveal an information mismatch, not to test loyalty or secure a reassuring promise. If access is still pending, identify that state and who can resolve it. Asking for permission is not proof that access has been granted.

Repair an omission you own and inform affected people. Take access or shift constraints to the responsible person instead of assuming all failures are yours. Willingness to accept work and practical ability to execute it also need separate confirmation. One recount does not guarantee flawless performance; later changes still require communication.

### Original cover example: a discussion is not an approved replacement

A colleague becomes unavailable and you want to reassure a supervisor that someone will cover. Before giving that assurance, establish:

- Which work needs coverage?
- Which hours need an available person?
- Which qualifications are required?
- Who can approve the arrangement?
- Who is willing and has actual capacity this time?

 Helping previously does not establish current agreement, and being open to discussing a shift is not confirmed cover. Before confirmation you can offer to check; you cannot promise unknown staffing or results.

If you can prepare materials but cannot take the whole shift, state that scope and the remaining gap. Bring it to the person able to decide staffing rather than treating your confidence as evidence that resources exist. Report an unavailable arrangement honestly. Do not make a necessary obligation sound optional or use personal loyalty to demand extra work.

Refusing an unreasonable request can coexist with checking alternatives. Explore actual tasks, independent judgment, qualifications, training, maintenance and recovery conditions when considering a career. The suffix does not prove fitness for management or service, nor exclude technical or analytical work.
sections.title: Work and career exploration

sections.body_md:
### Original birthday example: public recognition needs permission this time

You plan public birthday recognition because you expect a relative to feel included, but they prefer privacy. Ask what is welcome now: a private message, later contact, no public naming or no event. Last year's approval or a friendly response once does not establish this year's consent. They need not demonstrate gratitude before you respect that preference. Do not publicize their private reasons to explain the change.

If recognition has not happened, cancel or change it to an agreed form. If a stated boundary was already crossed, acknowledge the specific effect and, where appropriate, remove information where removal is possible, correct a misunderstanding or alter the next arrangement. Time and money already spent can be discussed without making participation an emotional debt. Immediate forgiveness cannot be required to prove that your good intentions worked.

You can still explain why contact matters and make an answerable request. Respecting a different form does not require denying your own needs. The useful conversation concerns both people's choices, not which personality supposedly likes gifts best.

### Your calm cannot close another person's concern

After a disagreement you may be ready for ordinary conversation while the other person still wants to address missing information, unwanted disclosure, a broken agreement or another form of contact. Ask which issue remains. Your settled feeling cannot declare it resolved for both of you, but taking responsibility does not require endless self-blame either.

State what you can repair, current limits and a workable time to revisit. If they do not want to talk now, respect the timing while still handling an already clear obligation. Silence cannot establish agreement or forgiveness. If they have clearly said there is no further issue, repeated requests for reassurance are unnecessary unless a genuine new fact arises.

Include notification, reminders and changed plans in shared responsibilities. Ask specifically for appreciation, shared work or rest rather than expecting others to infer it. Consent, kept agreements and repair are more informative than who recovers faster or whether the letters form an ideal pairing.
sections.title: Relationships and communication

sections.body_md:
### Original absence example: composure does not supply resources

A co-organizer becomes unavailable and you immediately offer to take over. List the remaining work and which part you can actually accept. In this fictional small-event example, different obligations need different checks:

| Remaining work | Conditions to verify | Relevant action and its limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send changed information to participants | Current details, recipients, timing and an accepted sender | Prioritize necessary information; sent is not proof that a critical receipt problem is solved |
| Add optional decoration | Time, resources and whether it can genuinely be dropped | Reduce or defer it; extra decoration cannot replace missing instructions |
| Fulfill promised staffing | Qualifications, available people and decision authority | Confirm cover or report the gap promptly; an unconfirmed replacement is not a solution |

Priorities depend on actual duties and circumstances, not just which task you enjoy. Taking part can help without turning a resource shortage into a moral demand to do everything alone. Tell affected people early and offer an adjustment that can actually be approved. Maintaining a reassuring appearance cannot justify an unverified promise.

### Review specific effects without discarding your self-trust

Distinguish completed work, open work, your omissions, external constraints and approaches that proved usable. A missed reminder needs information or repair; absent staffing needs a resource decision; dislike of decoration is another question. General enjoyment cannot prove that all three were addressed, and praise cannot cancel an unfulfilled agreement.

Plan rest and an accepted handover. A review endpoint can stop repetitive polishing or rumination, but it cannot make an important error or unfinished duty disappear. A new material fact still requires an update. Calm, worry and needing help are not moral rankings. Persistent distress affecting daily life deserves attention to actual causes and appropriate support; A cannot measure health, workload tolerance or need for assistance.
sections.title: Pressure and recovery

sections.body_md:
### Original document-handoff record: check the offer in use

Choose a low-risk handoff you can adjust, without experimenting with safety, medical decisions or another person's rights. This is an educational observation example, not an A/T test or a validated improvement program.

1. **Specify the purpose.** The new colleague needs current event instructions and a contact for questions; that differs from proving that your arrangement is good. List necessary information before adding extra work.
2. **Check the route and the recipient's choice.** Ask whether they can access the material, when receipt is workable and what they want to handle themselves. Private reasons need not be disclosed to request another time or contact.
3. **Make a bounded commitment.** State which current documents you will provide, when and who will check pending access. A choice of delivery method does not make a genuine work requirement optional; explain both clearly.
4. **Hear a specific objection.** An inaccessible link needs an access check; a preference for another layout can be evaluated against purpose. Separate them before defending the arrangement. Repeating how considerate it was cannot repair the link.
5. **Check actual states.** Record receipt, understanding of critical information and accepted responsibility. An access request is still pending; missing material cannot be marked complete. Give open issues to a responsible person who actually accepts them.
6. **Retain useful parts and a counterexample.** Correct a concrete gap, keep what is usable and avoid repeated changes without new information. Also record when you felt uncertain, your initiative added an unwanted burden or someone else was better placed to handle it.

The record informs this task without proving that help always works or that you are Assertive. Review practical completion separately from self-evaluation before deciding what to keep. Read the base profile for all four preferences and their qualified theory, or the comparison for possible responses to the same event.

### Original filled record: an access request is still an open state

This hypothetical document handoff is not evidence of a real task result.

- **Barrier:** the worker cannot view the old group. A permission request has been sent, but access has not been confirmed.
- **Action:** the responsible person checks an authorized route or backup contact. State the current limitation rather than expanding access without authority.
- **Separate checks:** suppose the worker confirms receiving the current instructions, recounts the critical time and accepts a task within capacity. Receipt, understanding and agreement are three answers; a polite “OK” cannot fill all of them.
- **Open issue:** extra staffing remains unapproved. Name the gap and decision-maker; forwarding the request does not establish that someone accepted handling it.
- **Your repair:** if you omitted the new time, correct it and inform those affected. The access barrier does not cancel that responsibility.

In a real record, missing receipt or usability evidence leaves an unknown result. Keep a method that works after this handoff; communicate a concrete new change without repeatedly seeking praise or skipping it to appear composed.

sections.body_md:
The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; shared letters do not make different tests equivalent. Type narratives and cognitive functions are theoretical interpretations, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not identify a representative country sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types and found overlap with dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument editions and samples matter: the publisher reports later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of a FermatMind score. That specific study does not validate these scenarios, determine an individual's type or settle every question about later instruments.

A newer review by Erford and colleagues (2025) synthesized 193 studies using English-language MBTI Form M, published during 1999–2024. It reported favorable internal-consistency estimates (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence, while finding no independent structural-validity or test–retest studies in its eligible literature beyond the manual. Score consistency does not establish distinct natural types, validate A/T, or transfer to FermatMind. Both supportive findings and remaining gaps depend on the specific instrument and samples.

The situations and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or findings about groups. Compare them with your experience, including counterexamples. Do not use type alone to diagnose, hire, choose a career or screen a relationship.

Content revised 8 October 2026. This is a source-based educational synthesis, not a claim of independent clinical review.

- [MBTI facts](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts)
- [16Personalities framework](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory)
- [McCrae & Costa (1989), study abstract](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1458465)
- [Erford et al. (2025), Form M psychometric synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcad.70006)
- [MBTI ethical use](https://www.myersbriggs.org/using-type-as-a-professional/mbti-code-of-ethics/home.htm)

The [original Identity description](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) supports the source and self-assurance vocabulary of A/T, not the effects of these original examples, a same-day recovery deadline or demonstrated arranging skill. [Official type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) describes proposed four-letter process roles and acknowledges the tertiary-attitude disagreement; it does not measure A/T. The observation tables, handoff, cover, birthday and absence examples are original. Their practical questions concern information, agreement, resources and responsibility rather than group statistics.

Do not make a necessary obligation sound optional or use personal loyalty to demand extra work.

Refusing an unreasonable request can coexist with checking alternatives. Explore actual tasks, independent judgment, qualifications, training, maintenance and recovery conditions when considering a career. The suffix does not prove fitness for management or service, nor exclude technical or analytical work.
sections.title: Work and career exploration

sections.body_md:
### Original birthday example: public recognition needs permission this time

You plan public birthday recognition because you expect a relative to feel included, but they prefer privacy. Ask what is welcome now: a private message, later contact, no public naming or no event. Last year's approval or a friendly response once does not establish this year's consent. They need not demonstrate gratitude before you respect that preference. Do not publicize their private reasons to explain the change.

If recognition has not happened, cancel or change it to an agreed form. If a stated boundary was already crossed, acknowledge the specific effect and, where appropriate, remove information where removal is possible, correct a misunderstanding or alter the next arrangement. Time and money already spent can be discussed without making participation an emotional debt. Immediate forgiveness cannot be required to prove that your good intentions worked.

You can still explain why contact matters and make an answerable request. Respecting a different form does not require denying your own needs. The useful conversation concerns both people's choices, not which personality supposedly likes gifts best.

### Your calm cannot close another person's concern

After a disagreement you may be ready for ordinary conversation while the other person still wants to address missing information, unwanted disclosure, a broken agreement or another form of contact. Ask which issue remains. Your settled feeling cannot declare it resolved for both of you, but taking responsibility does not require endless self-blame either.

State what you can repair, current limits and a workable time to revisit. If they do not want to talk now, respect the timing while still handling an already clear obligation. Silence cannot establish agreement or forgiveness. If they have clearly said there is no further issue, repeated requests for reassurance are unnecessary unless a genuine new fact arises.

Include notification, reminders and changed plans in shared responsibilities. Ask specifically for appreciation, shared work or rest rather than expecting others to infer it. Consent, kept agreements and repair are more informative than who recovers faster or whether the letters form an ideal pairing.
sections.title: Relationships and communication

sections.body_md:
### Original absence example: composure does not supply resources

A co-organizer becomes unavailable and you immediately offer to take over. List the remaining work and which part you can actually accept. In this fictional small-event example, different obligations need different checks:

| Remaining work | Conditions to verify | Relevant action and its limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send changed information to participants | Current details, recipients, timing and an accepted sender | Prioritize necessary information; sent is not proof that a critical receipt problem is solved |
| Add optional decoration | Time, resources and whether it can genuinely be dropped | Reduce or defer it; extra decoration cannot replace missing instructions |
| Fulfill promised staffing | Qualifications, available people and decision authority | Confirm cover or report the gap promptly; an unconfirmed replacement is not a solution |

Priorities depend on actual duties and circumstances, not just which task you enjoy. Taking part can help without turning a resource shortage into a moral demand to do everything alone. Tell affected people early and offer an adjustment that can actually be approved. Maintaining a reassuring appearance cannot justify an unverified promise.

### Review specific effects without discarding your self-trust

Distinguish completed work, open work, your omissions, external constraints and approaches that proved usable. A missed reminder needs information or repair; absent staffing needs a resource decision; dislike of decoration is another question. General enjoyment cannot prove that all three were addressed, and praise cannot cancel an unfulfilled agreement.

Plan rest and an accepted handover. A review endpoint can stop repetitive polishing or rumination, but it cannot make an important error or unfinished duty disappear. A new material fact still requires an update. Calm, worry and needing help are not moral rankings. Persistent distress affecting daily life deserves attention to actual causes and appropriate support; A cannot measure health, workload tolerance or need for assistance.
sections.title: Pressure and recovery

sections.body_md:
### Original document-handoff record: check the offer in use

Choose a low-risk handoff you can adjust, without experimenting with safety, medical decisions or another person's rights. This is an educational observation example, not an A/T test or a validated improvement program.

1. **Specify the purpose.** The new colleague needs current event instructions and a contact for questions; that differs from proving that your arrangement is good. List necessary information before adding extra work.
2. **Check the route and the recipient's choice.** Ask whether they can access the material, when receipt is workable and what they want to handle themselves. Private reasons need not be disclosed to request another time or contact.
3. **Make a bounded commitment.** State which current documents you will provide, when and who will check pending access. A choice of delivery method does not make a genuine work requirement optional; explain both clearly.
4. **Hear a specific objection.** An inaccessible link needs an access check; a preference for another layout can be evaluated against purpose. Separate them before defending the arrangement. Repeating how considerate it was cannot repair the link.
5. **Check actual states.** Record receipt, understanding of critical information and accepted responsibility. An access request is still pending; missing material cannot be marked complete. Give open issues to a responsible person who actually accepts them.
6. **Retain useful parts and a counterexample.** Correct a concrete gap, keep what is usable and avoid repeated changes without new information. Also record when you felt uncertain, your initiative added an unwanted burden or someone else was better placed to handle it.

The record informs this task without proving that help always works or that you are Assertive. Review practical completion separately from self-evaluation before deciding what to keep. Read the base profile for all four preferences and their qualified theory, or the comparison for possible responses to the same event.

### Original filled record: an access request is still an open state

This hypothetical document handoff is not evidence of a real task result.

- **Barrier:** the worker cannot view the old group. A permission request has been sent, but access has not been confirmed.
- **Action:** the responsible person checks an authorized route or backup contact. State the current limitation rather than expanding access without authority.
- **Separate checks:** suppose the worker confirms receiving the current instructions, recounts the critical time and accepts a task within capacity. Receipt, understanding and agreement are three answers; a polite “OK” cannot fill all of them.
- **Open issue:** extra staffing remains unapproved. Name the gap and decision-maker; forwarding the request does not establish that someone accepted handling it.
- **Your repair:** if you omitted the new time, correct it and inform those affected. The access barrier does not cancel that responsibility.

In a real record, missing receipt or usability evidence leaves an unknown result. Keep a method that works after this handoff; communicate a concrete new change without repeatedly seeking praise or skipping it to appear composed.

items.answer: No. Official MBTI uses four preference pairs; Assertive is additional self-assurance language in extensions such as NERIS, whose Identity is not an official fifth preference. FermatMind's related notation does not make questions, scores or validity equivalent. Identify the tool you used and treat the page as reflection prompts, not a formal ability or health conclusion.
items.question: Is ESFJ-A an official MBTI classification?

items.answer: That is not established. Confidence does not demonstrate decision skill, authority, accurate understanding of people or performance. In the cover example, confirmed tasks, qualifications, willing staffing and approval are more informative than an assurance that everything will work. Evaluate real duties and sustained feedback; A/T cannot rank leadership potential or screen candidates.
items.question: Is ESFJ-A better suited to leadership than ESFJ-T?

items.answer: No such conclusion follows. Self-assurance can coexist with concern, and less visible worry is not proof of indifference. Check whether stated needs are heard, refusal is respected and actual effects are addressed. In the birthday example, allowing private recognition is observable; feeling that your intentions were generous cannot substitute for permission.
items.question: Does being Assertive mean an ESFJ does not care?

items.answer: Yes. Habits, personal obligations and authority differences can affect refusal independently of a suffix. List the work you can accept and verify who actually accepts the remainder. Seek feasible support where power constraints are real rather than blaming everything on insufficient confidence. One acceptance or refusal cannot verify A/T, and different parts of each description may fit different circumstances.
items.question: Can I recognize this description and still struggle to refuse help requests?

items.answer: Not on the evidence presented. Fe is a theoretical account of interpersonal and shared values, not a measure of empathy maturity or mind-reading. Tertiary Ne/Ni also has competing attitude interpretations explained in the base profile. A/T belongs to a different framework, adds no function and does not settle those evidential issues. Understanding a person still requires checking present needs and permission.
items.question: Does ESFJ-A have more developed Fe?

items.answer: Yes. E concerns orientation rather than being social at every moment; F concerns values and human consequences rather than prohibiting logic. A does not restrict interests. Compare preferences and exceptions across contexts, separating role demands, experience and real choices. One solitary or analytical activity cannot settle a code; the base profile provides the fuller definitions.
items.question: Can ESFJ-A enjoy solitary work and logical analysis?

items.answer: No ranking of growth follows from the label. Different tools, versions, circumstances, question interpretation, measurement variation or actual change can contribute; the label cannot distinguish them. Compare the tool, timing and concrete experiences first. Even a repeat result on the same instrument cannot automatically turn A-to-T into regression, worsening health or reduced ability.
items.question: Does a later T result mean I have regressed?

items.answer: Read the base ESFJ profile for four preferences and qualified function theory, the A/T comparison for possible responses to one event, or ESFJ-T for the more self-questioning account. In a real task, check need, permission, receipt, accepted responsibility and open issues. The test entry can support further reflection but does not replace occupational, relationship or health judgment.
items.question: Which ESFJ page should I read next?

sections.body_md:
The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; shared letters do not make different tests equivalent. Type narratives and cognitive functions are theoretical interpretations, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not identify a representative country sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types and found overlap with dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument editions and samples matter: the publisher reports later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of a FermatMind score. That specific study does not validate these scenarios, determine an individual's type or settle every question about later instruments.

A newer review by Erford and colleagues (2025) synthesized 193 studies using English-language MBTI Form M, published during 1999–2024. It reported favorable internal-consistency estimates (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence, while finding no independent structural-validity or test–retest studies in its eligible literature beyond the manual. Score consistency does not establish distinct natural types, validate A/T, or transfer to FermatMind. Both supportive findings and remaining gaps depend on the specific instrument and samples.

The situations and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or findings about groups. Compare them with your experience, including counterexamples. Do not use type alone to diagnose, hire, choose a career or screen a relationship.

Content revised 8 October 2026. This is a source-based educational synthesis, not a claim of independent clinical review.

- [MBTI facts](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts)
- [16Personalities framework](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory)
- [McCrae & Costa (1989), study abstract](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1458465)
- [Erford et al. (2025), Form M psychometric synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcad.70006)
- [MBTI ethical use](https://www.myersbriggs.org/using-type-as-a-professional/mbti-code-of-ethics/home.htm)

The [original Identity description](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) supports the source and self-assurance vocabulary of A/T, not the effects of these original examples, a same-day recovery deadline or demonstrated arranging skill. [Official type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) describes proposed four-letter process roles and acknowledges the tertiary-attitude disagreement; it does not measure A/T. The observation tables, handoff, cover, birthday and absence examples are original. Their practical questions concern information, agreement, resources and responsibility rather than group statistics.
